title: A highly-sensitive and rapid Surface Plasmon Resonance immunoassay procedure based on the covalent-orientated immobilization of antibodies
protocol: Incubate the Au-coated SPR chip with Au surface cleaning solution for two minutes.
Wash the cleaned Au-coated SPR chip extensively with DIW.
Incubate the cleaned Au-coated SPR chip with 100 µL of 2% \(v/v) APTES for 1 hour at room temperature in a fume hood.
Wash the incubated SPR chip five times with DIW.
Incubate PrA (990µL of 100 µg/ml in HBS) with cross-linking solution containing EDC (4 mg/mL) and sulfoNHS (11 mg/mL) in 0.1 M MES buffer, pH 4.7, at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Inject fifty microliters of EDC-sulfoNHS activated PrA (100 µg/mL) over all four flow cells of an APTES-functionalized Au chip at a flow rate of 10 µL/min.
Inject 20 μl of 1% (w/v) BSA for blocking.
Use filtered BSA or filter the BSA solution before use to remove contaminants.
Inject 50 µL of anti-HFA antibody at a concentration of 100 µg/mL in 10 mM HBS, pH 7.4, over all flow cells at a flow rate of 10 μL/min.
Pass 50 µL of dilution buffer (10mM HBS, pH 7.4) through all flow cells before HFA capture and record the changes in SPR response units (RU).
Inject 50 µL of HFA at six different concentrations (0.6, 1.2, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, and 20.0 ng/mL) through the flow cells.
Subtract RU values obtained for blanks from the RU values for HFA detected in respective flow cells.
Plot SPR-based HFA detection curves using SigmaPlot software version 11.2 with standard curve analysis based on a four parameter logistic function.
Generate analytical parameters such as EC50 and Hillslope using the software analysis report.
